title: Pesto Pasta with Green Beans
subtitle: Classic Ligurian spaghetti with fresh basil pesto
excerpt: Spaghetti tossed with a vibrant homemade basil pesto and briefly blanched green beans, cooked together in the same pot. This is the traditional Ligurian way of serving pesto pasta.
sourceNotes: Pesto alla genovese comes from Genoa in Liguria. The traditional version is made with a pestle and mortar. Adding green beans and potato to the pasta is a classic Ligurian technique that stretches the dish and adds texture.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The pesto can be made up to 3 days ahead. Keep in a jar with a layer of olive oil on top.

content.text: Never toss pesto pasta over heat. The basil turns black and the pesto splits. Always add the pesto off the heat, using plenty of pasta water to create a sauce.
Make the pesto. Put the basil, garlic, pine nuts, parmesan, lemon zest, and olive oil in a food processor.
Pulse until just combined. The texture should be slightly rough, not completely smooth. Season with salt.
Cook the spaghetti in well-salted boiling water.
Add the green beans to the pasta water for the last 4 minutes of cooking.
Scoop out a large mugful of pasta water before draining.
Drain the spaghetti and beans. Return to the pan off the heat.
Add the pesto and a generous splash of pasta water.
Toss well. Add more pasta water until the sauce coats the spaghetti loosely.
Add a squeeze of lemon juice. Serve with extra parmesan.

items.cause: The basil was blended too long and the heat from the motor oxidised it.
items.fix: Pulse in short bursts and stop as soon as it comes together.

items.symptom: Sauce is too thick and clings in clumps.
items.cause: Not enough pasta water was used to loosen it.
items.fix: Keep adding pasta water a splash at a time until it flows.
